newsitem.title: PERU: SOCCER-PERU PROTEST TO FIFA OVER REFEREE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PERU PROTEST TO FIFA OVER REFEREE.

text.p: Peru have protested to international soccer's governing body FIFA over the refereeing of their World Cup qualifying match away to Uruguay last Sunday.

Peruvian Football Federation president Jose Aramburu said on Tuesday that a letter had been sent to FIFA complaining about a decision to disallow a goal by Peru striker Roberto Palacios for handball when Uruguay were leading 1-0.

Aramburu said the goal happened at a crucial moment as it came immediately after Enzo Francescoli had missed a penalty for Uruguay. Seven minutes later, Pablo Bengoechea scored Uruguay's second in their 2-0 win.
Palacios said on Tuesday: "I did not at any moment touch the ball with my hand."
Palacios's striking partner Flavio Maestri claimed that Colombian referee Felipe Russi admitted his alleged mistake to several Peruvian players later in the game.
He added that referees in general did not respect Peru because they never complained. "Peru never says anything," he said.

Peru, who have only won one of their six games, are seventh in the nine team South American group although only three points separate them from third-placed Argentina. The top four qualify for the World Cup finals in France.
Peru have not qualified for the finals since 1982.
